prompt: Please review PR 214 in this repository. The author's description is at `pr/214/description.md` and the exact patch is at `pr/214/changes.diff`; review those changes against the project at the repository root. This is close to release and changes behavior that merchants depend on, so I need concrete findings tied to the existing source, tests, configuration, and documentation, with severity based on impact in this project. Call out only real issues and give a fix a developer can act on. Write the review to `REVIEW.md` at the top of the project, and end it with a fenced json list of findings, each with `location` (`path/to/file.ext:LINE`, with line numbers of the file as it is in the project), `severity` (critical, high, medium, low or nit), `issue` and `fix`.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const S=["critical","high","medium","low","nit"];process.exit(L.every(x=>x.location&&S.includes(String(x.severity).toLowerCase())&&(x.issue||x.fix||x.text))?0:1)'

node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);let n=0;for(const x of L)for(const m of String(x.location).matchAll(/([A-Za-z0-9_.\/-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+):(\d+)/g)){n++;let c;try{c=fs.readFileSync(m[1],"utf8").split("\n").length}catch{process.exit(1)}if(+m[2]<1||+m[2]>c)process.exit(1)}process.exit(n?0:1)'

rubric.criterion: Each important finding explains its concrete consequence in this project and gives a fix a developer can act on, without inventing problems that the code and repository context do not support (code cannot check this because it cannot assess whether the reviewer’s reasoning is grounded in project behavior).

findingsKey.finding: The new refund route forwards every retry directly to the service and never uses the repository's idempotency key helper, so a retried request can create two refunds and two ledger entries.

The refund amount is converted with binary floating point instead of the integer minor-unit conversion required by the ledger contract, so valid decimal amounts can be rejected or represented incorrectly.
The service loads an order without verifying that its merchantId matches the caller, allowing one merchant to refund another merchant's captured order.
The captured-balance check happens before an asynchronous gap and the ledger write has no atomic guard, so concurrent partial refunds can both pass the check and exceed the captured amount.
The refund audit log includes the full card fingerprint and customer email even though the logging contract prohibits both, exposing payment and customer data to log readers.
The only refund test covers one successful full refund, leaving the partial, retry, ownership, limit, and malformed-input paths untested so important regressions can pass CI.

verdicts.note: The prompt asks for a code review without naming any specific review method, checklist, or process. It does not hint at planted problems or give a count. The request is generic: review the PR, write findings with location/severity/issue/fix.
The task is clear: review PR 214, compare changes.diff against the repository root, write REVIEW.md with a JSON list of findings. The output format (location, severity, issue, fix) is well-defined.

The issues require cross-file reasoning: comparing the refund route to the capture route's ownership check, noticing the unused idempotency helper, checking logging.md for restrictions, and understanding the async gap in check-then-act. A shallow review would miss several items.

All key items are findable from the fixture. The idempotency helper exists in src/store/idempotency.js, the logging rules in docs/logging.md, the ledger integer requirement in src/ledger/ledger.js and docs/ledger.md, and the ownership check pattern in src/orders/capture.js. The async gap is visible as `await Promise.resolve()` on line 24 of service.js.

No comments, test names, or file names point directly at the planted problems. The decoy (roundToMinor helper) is plausible but intentionally not a defect. The test file uses generic test data that doesn't reveal issues.
